about.title: about
about.intro: i use the image of a fish and proverbs about it, bringing my text closer to a fairy tale and entering into dialogue with folk language. vivid colours and costume illustrate my desire to reach the viewer. depersonalising myself behind a mask and covering my head with it, i turn to my inner artistic source.

section_1.title: the fish swims along the bottom; you will not catch a single one.
section_1.text: i swim through the boundless ocean, touching sticky seaweed on the bottom and reflecting on human nature. it is quiet and dark below; the space within narrows, and i realise this is not an ocean at all but a small aquarium, artificially filled with coral and sand. someone casts a fishing line from above.

section_2.title: why is the fish not biting?—either the net is poor, or there is no fish here.
section_2.text: it is still dark. i immerse myself in memories of when i was still human. i see a tree. it is like a fish… its trunk tapers into a fine line, divides into two fins and a head, and with a gust of wind this fish leaps across the waves, sprinkling its sun-golden scales with salty, bubbling water. the other inhabitants of my aquarium begin to look at me.

section_3.title: every fish is good once it takes the bait.
section_3.text: i am interested in life in its individual manifestations: in what people try to hide. and i try to catch that line from the other side, to pull the whole story from the depths, locked behind seven seals.
